## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">About Me
• Dr. Damian Betebenner, Senior Associate Center for Assessment
• Working with more than 30 states over the last two decades to
 develop models of academic student growth
• Working with Indiana for about a decade to develop several different
 models of student academic growth
• Currently advising about 15 states on their use of academic student
 growth during the COVID-19 pandemic

9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 2</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">COVID-19: The Situation
 • Global pandemic
 • Education interrupted worldwide with widespread cancellation of in person
 education in the US beginning in March, 2020
 • Nationwide suspension of state summative testing and accountability for
 2019-2020 school year
 • Unclear about the scope and format of K-12 education for the 2020-2021
 school year even as Fall 2020 is upon us
 • Lack of clarity on state summative testing and accountability for 2020-2021
 including the use and calculation of academic student growth

9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 3</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Current work with Indiana
 • Due to the cancellation of ILEARN testing this year (and the waiver for
 accountability), no student growth was calculated in 2020
 • Assuming the ILEARN is given in 2021, there are questions as to how
 accountability will be calculated
 • Annual growth (from 2020 to 2021) will not be calculable due to the absence
 of 2020 test data
 • Many states are considering using skip-year growth (2019 to 2021) in lieu of
 one-year growth
 • In place of running standard one-year growth analyses in 2020, the Indiana
 DOE asked me to run skip-year growth on historical ISTEP+ data to see how
 well it matches with one-year growth
 • A draft report of that investigation is currently under review by the INDOE
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 4</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Report Spoiler Alert
• Should Indiana calculate student growth? Yes!
 • The calculation of student growth has never been more important than now.
 • Student growth can be used in dozens of ways (not usually done for accountability) to
 help schools, districts, states assess and ameliorate the impact of COVID-19.
• Should Indiana use student growth for education accountability in 2021?
 Problematic!
 • Need to substitute skip-year growth (two-year growth from 2019 to 2021) for usual
 one-year growth.
 • Besides school interruption in Spring 2020, students’ education will be non-normal
 and disparate in the 2020-2021 academic year -- likely impacting opportunity to learn.
 • There are more beneficial applications of student growth for the coming year than
 just typical school accountability

9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 5</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Skip Year Growth Calculation
• Assuming ILEARN summative testing occurs as usual in Spring 2021,
 calculating skip-year growth from 2019 to 2021 should be fairly
 routine
• Student growth cohorts in most states will be:
 • ELA and Math Grade 3 to 5, 4 to 6, 5 to 7, 6 to 8
• Additional priors from 2018 can be used
• Interpretation may be far from routine
 • Two-year academic student growth instead of a single year
 • Growth for 4th graders won’t exist because of no prior test from 2019
 • Might need to create two-year growth matrix values
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 6</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Skip Year Growth Calculation
• There are a couple of ways that state testing might not occur as usual
 in 2021.
 • Testing might be cancelled as it was in 2020. No testing in 2021 means no
 calculation of skip-year growth.
 • Testing might only occur with a (non-random) subset of the entire population
 of students.
 • State tests might be modified to accommodate pandemic related constraints
 in 2021 (e.g., abbreviated forms).
 • Some other option between no-test and census testing.
• Our discussion assumes some sort of testing takes place in Spring
 2021.
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 7</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Using skip-year in lieu of one-year
growth: Historical Results
• We didn’t find systematic differences between the group of students
 with one-year growth and those with skip-year growth.
• Skip-year growth and one-year growth scores are highly correlated at the
 individual level (~ 0.9).
• When aggregated to the school-level, growth scores for schools are
 highly correlated (~0.92).
• The high correlations mask differences for a substantial number of
 students/schools that would change interpretation.
• Currently re-running historical school grades to determine impact on
 those.
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 8</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Using skip-year in lieu of one-year
growth: Historical Results
• Historical analyses indicate that even under normal circumstances, it is
 tenuous to replace one-year growth with skip-year growth
• By any measure, current circumstances are far from normal
• Under current circumstances, it would likely be highly problematic to
 replace one-year growth with skip-year growth
• Students are receiving disparate educational experiences (remote, in-
 person, hybrid/concurrent) of disparate quality which will likely greatly
 impact student growth
• We won’t know for sure until 2021 data arrives but given what I know
 today, I would be skeptical that skip-year growth will be suitable for
 “business as usual” accountability in 2021
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 9</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/10.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Going beyond accountability with
growth
• Skip-year growth data in 2021 opens the door to numerous analytic
 investigations that go beyond accountability calculations performed by
 Indiana.
• Two critical investigative tracks states can pursue:
 • Investigate differential impact on student learning for various student groups.
 • Investigate the overall impact on student learning for the state and for various
 student groups.

9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 10</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/11.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Going beyond accountability with
growth
• For SGP a common investigative technique is to look at “growth gaps”: Group mean/median
 SGP differences to identify issues worth investigating more deeply.
 • Issues related to opportunity to learn can be examined by looking at growth gaps for relevant
 demographic subgroups.
 • Issues related to program efficacy can be examined by looking at growth gaps for relevant groups
 receiving different “treatments”.
 • With good meta-data associated with student education in the 2020-2021 school year it’s possible to
 examine differential growth of students subjected to remote versus in person learning.
• Extending this idea, states can compare growth gaps over time (i.e., skip-year growth gaps in
 2019 versus skip-year growth gaps in 2021) to examine whether growth gaps have waned or
 extended with the COVID-19 pandemic.
 • In most states there has always been a growth gap between FRL/non-FRL. Has the growth-gap widened?
 Is it the same in ELA and Mathematics? Is it the same across grades?
 • These ”over time” investigations will allow states to rigorously examine changes in opportunity to learn
 that have occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic.
• For SGPs, mean SGP group deviations of 5 correspond to an effect size of 0.18.
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 11</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/12.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Going beyond accountability with
growth
• A critical component of utilizing growth data to its potential is to have
 all the relevant grouping variables at your disposal.
• To investigate the impact of different 2020-2021 school/corporation
 implemented COVID-19 educational programs, one needs to know
 what those programs are.
 • Remote, hybrid, concurrent, in-person. These are likely to change throughout
 the year so observing these on multiple occasion is likely required.
 • COVID-19 postponement/cancellation at school requiring shift to remote
 learning.
 • School start day, number of days of instruction
• It’s critical to start preparing to collect this data NOW!
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 12</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/13.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Conclusions
• Based upon what I’m hearing/seeing nationally in terms of current
 schooling surveys, Indiana should be preparing for the worst in terms
 of impact on student learning (this is a Katrina-like event!)
• The impact on student learning is likely to be uneven but very bad for
 a substantial number of students
• The sooner Indiana can understand who these students are, the
 sooner interventions can occur.
• Student growth from 2019 to 2021 on the ILEARN will be late in
 arriving but critical in helping the state to understand where and how
 bad the impacts to student achievement are.
9/23/20 Indiana DOE Skip-Year Growth Report 13</div>
```
